previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis secondary to vasculitis, was admitted for worsening abdominal pain radiating to the back, associated with nausea and vomiting. She had recently been discharged after a similar episode. Initial management included NPO status for 48 hours to reduce gastrointestinal inflammation, followed by gradual advancement to a regular diet. Pain was controlled with IV and oral hydromorphone, and she was restarted on oral medications as tolerated. A PICC line was placed for medication and nutritional support, and she received parenteral nutrition. Esophagitis and gastritis were managed with a switch to pantoprazole, and a short prednisone taper was initiated for suspected vasculitis-related pain. She improved steadily, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for gastroenterology and nephrology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with recurrent pancreatitis presents with recurrent 
abdominal pain consistent with pancreatitis flare. 
.
PANCREATITIS, ACUTE
Her abdominal pain was similar in quality to her recurrent 
pancreatitis flares.  She may also have a component of 
gastritis.  She was treated with supportive measures, IV 
dilaudid, and IV fluids.  Her PPI was changed to IV famotidine.  
Given that she did not benefit from the prednisone that was 
started on prior admission, it was discontinued.  Over the 
course of 72 hrs her symptoms improved, her diet was advanced, 
and her regimen was changed to PO.  She will follow up with Dr. 
___ on ___.  Patient understands that a strategy must be 
devised to pre-empt her symptoms at home to avoid her very 
frequent admissions.
.
GASTRITIS, ACUTE
While the patient was NPO, her PPI was switched to IV famotidine 
(IV PPI allergy).  Her prednisone was also discontinued as it 
was thought to be exacerbating her symptoms and not alleviating 
her pancreatitis flare pain.  Her PPI was restarted on 
discharge.
.
DEPRESSION, NOS
Continued lexapro/amytryptiline once patient able to tolerate 
POs
.
TACHYCARDIA UNSPECIFIED: 
Continued betaxolol, fludracortisone
.
VASCULITIS NOS
Her prednisone was stopped given the reasons above.  Her MTX was 
continued.  ESR/CRP were checked and were normal.  She was urged 
to follow up with her PCP/Rheumatologist as soon as possible to 
discuss more aggressive treatment of her vasculitis as a cause 
of her symptoms.  Her plaquenil was restarted on discharge

your pancreatitis.  You improved with supportive measures.  The 
prednisone we had started last time was held given that it did 
not seem to benefit you.  We continued your methotrexate.  
Please resume all your previous medications as before.  You also 
have a UTI for which you will be given an antibiotic for 5 days.

well and prevent further admissions to the hospital.  Please

role that vasculitis is playing
